entity.summary: Global centralized cryptocurrency exchange launched July 14, 2017. On October 29, 2026, attackers compromised internal wallet-signing operations, causing unauthorized multi-chain transfers with an estimated USD 6.34 billion impact. Binance reported USD 2.85 billion frozen or intercepted; withdrawals began reopening in phases on November 1 while the investigation and restoration continued.
entity.notes: The October 29 attack and November 3 initial report are not separate hacks. Binance reported approximately 233.46 million XRP, 970,500 SOL, 44.2 million OP and 18,270 BTC moved to attacker-controlled addresses, followed by an EIP-7702 delegation attack on an Ethereum hot wallet. The last unauthorized 2,961.9 ETH transfer finalized at 23:56 UTC October 29, with the affected EIP-7702 authorization cleared at 00:10 UTC October 30, according to Binance. On October 31, the FBI attributed the incident to DPRK TraderTraitor actors; this is a law-enforcement attribution, not an independently completed HEI forensic investigation. Binance estimated USD 6.34B affected and USD 2.85B frozen/intercepted as of its November 3 report: frozen funds are not recovered funds, and the affected amount is not a final net unrecovered-loss figure. Binance's November 3 initial report said 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of October 31, whereas its November 1–2 recovery updates and November 3 management comments cited approximately 95%; the different reported percentages/cutoffs have not been independently reconciled. Remaining illiquid assets were still being purchased; replenishment and Proof of Reserves do not demonstrate recovery of stolen funds or final settlement of all claims. Global withdrawals began reopening November 1 and expanded November 3, but remained phased, supporting status=limited, not inactive or dead. Binance Japan stated its customers' separately held assets were unaffected, with local withdrawals also reopening in phases; regional entities must not be silently classified as direct victims. This is separate from Binance's May 2019 7,000 BTC breach and 2022/2024 regulatory penalties; no regulatory fine or compensation allocation is added to stolen-asset totals. The June-to-October social-engineering and internal-AI-tool narrative comes from Binance's preliminary report and remains subject to independent security review.

expected.summary: Centralized exchange launched in 2017 and still operating under the Binance brand.
expected.notes: Official Binance announcement set the exchange launch for 2017-07-14.

events.title: Binance entered coordinated U.S. criminal and civil resolutions
events.description: Binance Holdings pleaded guilty to U.S. anti-money-laundering, unlicensed money-transmitting, and sanctions violations and entered coordinated resolutions with DOJ, CFTC, FinCEN, and OFAC requiring more than USD 4.3 billion in aggregate penalties and compliance remediation.
events.notes: The CFTC consent order announced on this date was initially subject to court approval; this event records the coordinated resolution announcement and Binance guilty plea rather than a service shutdown.

events.title: U.S. prosecutors reportedly opened Iran-sanctions compliance probe into Binance
events.description: Bloomberg reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that federal prosecutors were investigating whether Binance violated U.S. sanctions on Iran and whether it knowingly allowed prohibited trading on its platform. Reuters reported that a source confirmed the probe.
events.notes: This records a reported investigation, not a charge, adjudication, or finding that Binance violated sanctions. Reuters reported that the Justice Department declined to comment. The event does not establish a shutdown or service limitation.

events.title: Binance reports unauthorized hot-wallet withdrawals affecting approximately USD 6.3 billion
events.description: On October 29 UTC, unauthorized asset transfers affected Binance-controlled wallets. In its October 30 initial investigation, Binance estimated the total impact at approximately USD 6.3 billion and said that around USD 3 billion in affected assets had been frozen on-chain. Binance attributed a possible initial compromise to a DevOps engineer's laptop and service-container access, but said no wallet private-key leak was found. The technical root cause, final loss, attribution and recovery remain under investigation.
events.amount_text: Approximately USD 6.3 billion estimated impact; approximately USD 3 billion frozen on-chain as of the October 30 statement
events.notes: The estimated affected amount is NOT a final net stolen or unrecovered loss. EIP-7702 transaction interpretations and actor-attribution claims require separate verification; the primary Binance statement identifies an initial hypothesis, not a completed post-mortem.

events.title: Binance temporarily pauses withdrawals; later confirms deposits remained available
events.description: Following unauthorized hot-wallet transfers on October 29, Binance suspended withdrawals for security checks and revoked affected address authorization. Its initial announcement also described a temporary deposits suspension, but a later official clarification stated that deposits remained unaffected and operating normally. Trading remained possible. Binance pledged to cover customer losses with SAFU and corporate resources, but compensation completion and full withdrawals reopening had not been established in the reviewed October 30 statements.
events.notes: The service restriction is not an exchange shutdown. The initial notice's deposits-and-withdrawals phrasing was subsequently corrected by Binance; use the latest clarified state rather than perpetuating a deposit freeze. Check withdrawal reopening independently and record its date before changing the exchange from limited to active.

events.title: Binance hot wallet loses 7,000 BTC in May 2019 security breach
events.description: Binance disclosed a May 7, 2019 security breach involving stolen API keys, 2FA codes and other potentially compromised information. It reported a single unauthorized withdrawal of 7,000 BTC from its BTC hot wallet (about 2% of Binance's BTC holdings), and pledged to cover affected user funds with its SAFU reserve. Reuters valued the BTC at approximately USD 41 million at the time. This historical exchange exploit is separate from the October 2026 incident.
events.amount_text: 7,000 BTC withdrawn; roughly USD 41 million at the May 2019 valuation
events.notes: 2019 and 2026 are separate exchange security incidents. Binance's pledge to cover customer losses is a contemporary statement, not a verified audit of reimbursement completion. Use BTC amount, not modern BTC prices, to represent the historical loss.

events.title: Dutch central bank imposes EUR 3.325 million registration penalty on Binance
events.description: De Nederlandsche Bank (DNB) imposed an administrative fine of EUR 3,325,000 on Binance Holdings Ltd. on April 25, 2022 for offering crypto services in the Netherlands without the mandatory local registration. DNB published the enforcement decision in July 2022 and said Binance indicated it would appeal. This regulatory penalty is distinct from security breaches and client asset losses.
events.notes: Fine imposed 2022-04-25; publicly announced 2022-07-18. Do not date the enforcement event to media publication or classify the fine as hacked funds.

events.title: Canada FINTRAC imposes CAD 6,002,000 administrative penalty on Binance
events.description: Canada's Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre (FINTRAC) imposed CAD 6,002,000 in administrative monetary penalties on Binance Holdings Limited on May 7, 2024 for failure to register as a foreign money services business and failure to report qualifying large virtual-currency transactions. The agency publicly announced the measure May 9; its notice said Binance appealed to Federal Court. Currency is CAD, not USD.
events.notes: Regulatory and compliance enforcement, not crypto stolen or a verified security incident. Fine was imposed May 7 and published May 9. Agency notice explicitly records an appeal.

events.title: India FIU imposes INR 188.2 million anti-money-laundering penalty on Binance
events.description: India's Financial Intelligence Unit imposed an administrative penalty totaling INR 188,200,000 (18.82 crore rupees) under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act on June 19, 2024. The FIU's Order-in-Original No. 10/DIR/FIU-IND/2024 describes breaches of reporting and compliance requirements. Reuters reported the event in June 2024. This regulatory enforcement must not be added to hacking or stolen-funds totals.
events.amount_text: INR 188,200,000 regulatory penalty (approximately USD 2.25 million at 2024 reporting FX rates)
events.notes: Primary order dated 2024-06-19, source published by India FIU. Currency basis INR, USD conversion is historical approximate, not a current FX conversion.

events.title: Binance says more than USD 6.34 billion allocated for incident remediation
events.description: Binance stated on October 30, 2026 that it had allocated more than USD 6.34 billion in company funds toward the October 29 wallet incident, including USD 5 billion already held in assets matching the affected tokens. It said it would acquire the remaining roughly USD 1.34 billion in corresponding assets through market or OTC channels. Binance separately described roughly USD 3 billion as frozen and excluded those freezes from the allocation total. This is a disclosed funding allocation and recovery commitment, not independent proof of cash balances, completed token purchases, final loss accounting or compensation paid to users.
events.amount_text: More than USD 6.34 billion company allocation claimed; USD 5B in matching token assets claimed; remaining approximately USD 1.34B in planned market/OTC purchases
events.notes: Do not sum the reported >USD 6.34B corporate allocation with estimated USD 3B frozen or initial affected-asset amount. Reuters corroborates publication of the claim, not independent audit of treasury or wallet balances. No change from limited to active until withdrawals actually resume.

events.title: Binance begins phased withdrawal restoration after October 29 breach
events.description: Binance announced phase-one reopening of withdrawals for selected networks and assets beginning November 1, 2026, after the October 29 hot-wallet compromise. The exchange expanded eligible assets and networks on November 3. Deposits remained operational, but full unrestricted withdrawal access was not yet established.
events.notes: Partial withdrawal recovery, not full normalization and not an exchange relaunch. Do not change global entity status to active until complete restoration is substantiated.

events.title: Binance releases initial technical findings on October 29 multi-chain wallet compromise
events.description: Binance stated that attackers abused access to an internal wallet signing service, enabling unauthorized transfers including approximately 233.46 million XRP, 970,500 SOL, 44.2 million OP and 18,270 BTC. The attackers also established malicious EIP-7702 delegation authorizations on Ethereum; Binance reported the final 2,961.9 ETH transfer finalized at 23:56 UTC October 29 and that revocation completed at 00:10 UTC October 30. Binance estimated USD 6.34 billion in affected assets and USD 2.85 billion frozen or intercepted; the FBI separately attributed the theft to DPRK TraderTraitor actors on October 31.
events.amount_text: USD 6.34 billion affected; USD 2.85 billion frozen or intercepted (Binance estimates)
events.notes: This is a material November 3 disclosure about the already-recorded October 29 hack, not a second loss event. Distinguish impact, freeze, recovery and token-asset replenishment. Binance's social-engineering/AI-tool attack path remains preliminary pending independent review. FBI attribution reflects a published law-enforcement conclusion.

evidence.title: Binance and CEO Plead Guilty to Federal Charges in $4B Resolution
evidence.notes: DOJ announcement of the Binance Holdings guilty plea, financial penalty, compliance monitor, and Changpeng Zhao plea and resignation.

evidence.title: Binance and Its CEO Agree to Pay $2.85 Billion for Willfully Evading U.S. Law
evidence.notes: CFTC announcement of the proposed consent order and the coordinated aggregate resolution exceeding USD 4.3 billion.

evidence.title: Binance official exchange platform
evidence.notes: Current official domain confirming continued global exchange operation.

evidence.title: DOJ Probing Binance Over Potential Iran Sanctions Violations
evidence.notes: Reports, citing people familiar with the matter, that SDNY prosecutors and the Justice Department criminal division were examining Binance's Iran-sanctions compliance and whether prohibited trading was knowingly allowed.

evidence.title: Binance faces US scrutiny over possible Iran sanctions violations, source says
evidence.notes: Reuters reports that a source confirmed the federal probe after Bloomberg's report and notes that DOJ declined to comment. This evidence supports the existence of the reported investigation, not a finding of sanctions violations.

evidence.title: Security Incident Update
evidence.notes: Primary source for preliminary incident mechanism, USD 6.3B estimate, USD 3B frozen, and compensation pledge; not conclusive proof of final loss or root cause.

evidence.title: Binance's possible hack triggers $3 billion freeze in crypto assets
evidence.notes: Independent contemporary reporting of Binance investigation and issuer freezes; amounts are evolving estimates.

evidence.title: Security Incident Update
evidence.notes: Primary security statement originally described deposit and withdrawal suspensions; Binance subsequently clarified deposits remained operational. See the October 30 official follow-up and case report for the correction. SAFU and company funds were pledged; no payment-completion proof supplied.

evidence.title: Binance pauses withdrawals as hackers suspected of stealing billions in crypto
evidence.notes: Independent report quotes Binance spokesperson acknowledging temporary withdrawals suspension across multiple networks.

evidence.title: Binance Security Breach Update
evidence.notes: Primary acknowledgment of one 7,000 BTC hot-wallet withdrawal, attack vectors and SAFU compensation pledge.

evidence.title: Hackers steal $41 million worth of bitcoin from Binance cryptocurrency exchange
evidence.notes: Contemporary independent reporting of 7,000 BTC and contemporaneous USD valuation; Reuters coverage, not a second on-chain audit.

evidence.title: Boete voor Binance Holdings Ltd. vanwege zonder registratie aanbieden van cryptodiensten
evidence.notes: Primary Dutch regulator states April 25 decision, amount, registration breach and appeal context.

evidence.title: Dutch central bank fines Binance 3.3 million euros
evidence.notes: Independent report confirms the regulator's historical enforcement decision.

evidence.title: Administrative monetary penalty imposed on Binance Holdings Limited
evidence.notes: Primary regulator enforcement summary: CAD 6,002,000, imposed May 7, Binance's Federal Court appeal.

evidence.title: FINTRAC imposes administrative monetary penalty on Binance Holdings Limited
evidence.notes: Primary Canadian regulator release listing two reporting/registration violations.

evidence.title: FIU-IND Compliance Orders: Binance Order-in-Original No. 10/DIR/FIU-IND/2024
evidence.notes: Primary regulator index confirms June 19, 2024 Binance order and its designation.

evidence.title: India financial watchdog imposes $2.25 million penalty on Binance
evidence.notes: Independent confirmation of INR 188.2 million and anti-money-laundering reporting scope.

evidence.title: Binance has begun recovering the affected assets for users
evidence.notes: Binance statement of >USD 6.34B company resource allocation, USD 5B in matching token assets, remaining OTC/market purchase plan and separately frozen USD 3B.

evidence.title: Binance sets aside over $6.34 billion to cover losses from attack
evidence.notes: Independent reporting on company resource-allocation announcement, not independent proof of the underlying balances.

evidence.title: Security Incident | Recovery Update #4: Withdrawals Resume in Phases
evidence.notes: Official phased withdrawal-reopening announcement, not an assertion of full service restoration.

evidence.title: Security Incident | Recovery Update #6: Withdrawals Reopen for More Assets
evidence.notes: Official expansion of the phased reopening on November 3; not proof that every chain and token is available.

evidence.title: 29 October 2026 Binance Security Incident: Initial Findings and Response Update
evidence.notes: Primary company technical narrative; preliminary investigation, not final independent root-cause audit. Reports impact, freeze, multi-chain quantities, EIP-7702 and revocation chronology.

evidence.title: North Korea Responsible for $6 Billion+ Binance Attack
evidence.notes: U.S. law-enforcement attribution of the October 29 theft to DPRK TraderTraitor; public attribution is distinct from independent reproduction of the full attack path.

evidence.title: Binance hackers used fake job interview in $6.3 billion attack
evidence.notes: Independent journalism reporting Binance's November 3 technical disclosure and FBI attribution; not an independent audit of company-provided numerical estimates.
